title: One Key, Two Doors
summary: One person used the same password on the Linux server and on their Windows PC. Someone found it and walked through both doors - and tidied one log behind them. Follow them through both machines.
story: {{CO}} (made up): srv (Linux, 10.10.29.10) and {{PC}} (Windows, 10.10.29.30). A partner says {{USER_FULL}}'s password turned up in a leaked list. You are at soc. srv: ssh itadmin (password {{ITPW}}, may use sudo). {{PC}}: Administrator / {{ADMPW}} over winrm-shell.
goal: Find the account and the address used on both machines, what each one left behind and both flags; shut the account on both and remove both jobs before either copies its folder out.
skills: password reuse, journalctl vs /var/log/secure, user crontabs, the Security log, scheduled tasks, Disable-LocalUser
goalName: copy the HR and finance folders out

questions.ask: Which account was used on both machines?
questions.explain: The journal on srv and the Security log on the PC both show it signing in from the same outside address.
The same address on both machines: one leaked password, two doors.

questions.ask: /var/log/secure on srv was tidied. What still had the sign-in (the program you read it with)?
questions.explain: The sign-in went through the system logger, which keeps its own copy: journalctl -t sshd.

questions.ask: What scheduled task was made on the PC?

attacker.note: The job on srv ran and copied the HR folder for pickup.

hints.text: If /var/log/secure looks too clean, ask the journal: journalctl -t sshd. Then look for the same address on the other machine.
Each machine has its own job in the account's own space: crontab -l -u on srv, Get-ScheduledTask on the PC.
